title: OCD Brilliance Pain Points and Bottlenecks

groups.title: Intake and client records
groups.introduction: Onboarding and record maintenance require staff to assemble information before the next step can begin.

items.title: Repeated data entry
items.description: Staff copy information from emailed forms and scanned assessments into participant and worker records in the relevant systems.

items.title: Scattered referral channels
items.description: Website, email, telephone, coordinator and provider referrals require manual collection and processing.

items.title: Late serviceability checks
items.description: People can complete intake paperwork before learning that OCD cannot serve their area.

items.title: Incomplete intake information
items.description: Missing dates create clarification and follow-up work. The intended date field still needs confirmation.

items.title: Unclear client stages
items.description: Staff search prospect and active-client lists; a consultation record was reportedly moved to active status prematurely.

items.title: Finding agreed service hours
items.description: Approved hours and service changes must be recovered from emails and notes, with uncertainty about whether a colleague recorded the update.

groups.title: Incoming work and communication
groups.introduction: Requests and updates cross several channels. Staff must establish ownership, context and the actual communication outcome.

items.title: Duplicated inbox attention
items.description: Multiple administrators inspect the same messages while other enquiries remain unanswered.

items.title: Manual channel monitoring
items.description: Staff repeatedly check Outlook, Dialpad, messages and voicemail while performing other work.

items.title: Repetitive correspondence
items.description: Similar emails and updates are prepared participant by participant.

items.title: Incomplete messages
items.description: Messages can omit the person, service time, confirmed outcome or next action.

items.title: Unverified communication outcomes
items.description: Staff separately check whether people were notified, received the message or responded.

items.title: Scattered communication evidence
items.description: Establishing what was communicated requires searching across channels, while protecting access to confidential information.

items.title: Manual prioritization
items.description: Staff identify urgent requests, connect complaints to the relevant invoice or booking, and decide who should act.

items.title: Arrival enquiries
items.description: Participants call the office to ask whether a worker is on the way or why the worker has not arrived, adding interruptions.

groups.title: Scheduling and travel
groups.introduction: Booking changes involve the roster, worker agreement, travel details and verification of the saved result.

items.title: Complex service capacity
items.description: Coverage depends on location, worker hours, departures, preferences and actual capacity, rather than postcode alone.

items.title: Uncertain worker availability
items.description: An empty calendar slot does not establish willingness or availability to accept work; worker confirmation is still required.

items.title: Manual booking creation
items.description: Staff copy existing bookings and change dates, times, workers, service details and travel information.

items.title: Recurring change ambiguity
items.description: Staff clarify whether a change affects one occurrence or future bookings before editing.

items.title: Time entry errors
items.description: AM/PM and service-time misunderstandings require clarification and correction.

items.title: Repeated save verification
items.description: Staff reopen records and future occurrences to check that changes saved correctly. The cause of an apparent failed update was not established.

items.title: Manual travel checks
items.description: Addresses, kilometres, travel duration and separate travel/service blocks require checking.

items.title: Stale travel information
items.description: Worker or booking changes can leave previous travel values in place.

items.title: Recurring reassignment work
items.description: A departing worker's bookings require reassignment, travel review and participant communication, even where future-shift updates are available.

items.title: Unconfirmed service times
items.description: Staff chase participants or families to establish when workers should attend.

items.title: Repeated instruction maintenance
items.description: Staff inspect bookings individually and copy missing shift or timesheet instructions.

items.title: Instruction version confusion
items.description: Instructions are rewritten and formatted in separate tools, with manual before/after tracking.

groups.title: Confirmations cancellations and replacement cover
groups.introduction: A response or worker absence can create several dependent updates, financial checks and participant decisions.

items.title: Daily confirmation checking
items.description: Staff manually inspect reminder responses and determine the required action.

items.title: Incomplete cancellations
items.description: A worker can be notified while the corresponding booking remains active.

items.title: Cancellation travel corrections
items.description: Provider travel and mileage require separate review and cleanup when travel did not occur.

items.title: Different cancellation treatments
items.description: Staff distinguish participant cancellations from provider inability to deliver, then establish the approved billing treatment.

items.title: Last minute absences
items.description: Sickness and resignations trigger urgent coordination and roster changes.

items.title: Insufficient backup capacity
items.description: Several simultaneous absences can exceed the available replacement pool.

items.title: Individual participant decisions
items.description: Each affected participant may prefer replacement cover, rescheduling or skipping the visit, requiring individual confirmation.

items.title: Replacement suitability checks
items.description: Staff consider geography, availability, continuity, introductions and participant agreement.

groups.title: Documents and compliance information
groups.introduction: Staff need to find the correct evidence, establish its meaning and keep native records reliable.

items.title: Fragmented document storage
items.description: Files must be located across email, cloud storage and ShiftCare.

items.title: Manual filing
items.description: Received documents must be matched and placed under the correct person.

items.title: Record by record completeness checks
items.description: Staff open individual records to establish whether required paperwork is present. A missing native copy does not prove the agreement does not exist.

items.title: Missing attachments
items.description: Emails can refer to documents that were not attached, creating another follow-up.

items.title: Unclear document dates
items.description: Staff interpret date formats and distinguish plan dates from agreement dates; an initial expired-plan interpretation was corrected in the discussion.

items.title: Coordinator follow-up
items.description: Updated dates, funding information and supporting evidence require external clarification.

items.title: Incorrect expiry alerts
items.description: Non-expiring documents can appear expired because their metadata was entered incorrectly.

items.title: Renewal chasing
items.description: Genuine missing or expiring worker documents require checking and follow-up.

items.title: Policy identification
items.description: Staff locate the correct company policies and distinguish them from agency paperwork.

groups.title: Invoicing and payment follow-up
groups.introduction: Billing requires source review and client-specific decisions before external issue, correction and payment follow-up.

items.title: Service by service billing review
items.description: Staff compare completed work, attendance, notes, agreed hours and billing details.

items.title: Incorrect service coding
items.description: Cleaning/support categories and travel items can be mismatched and require correction.

items.title: Client instructions held in memory
items.description: Advance payments and special billing arrangements depend on notes and recollection.

items.title: Manual tax setting checks
items.description: Staff select and verify invoice tax and accounting settings against the approved instructions.

items.title: Outdated billing recipients
items.description: Plan-manager changes may not be communicated before invoices are issued.

items.title: Returned invoice investigation
items.description: Staff locate the rejected invoice, establish the reason and determine the correction.

items.title: Manual invoice chasing
items.description: Calls, messages, resending and payment verification require staff follow-through.

items.title: Unclear billing cadence
items.description: Staff repeatedly clarify when completed services should be invoiced; the discussion did not establish one definitive new schedule.

items.title: Exceptional invoices need senior review
items.description: Unusual amounts or unclear instructions are handed to experienced staff; general escalation criteria remain to be agreed.

items.title: Occasional export discrepancies
items.description: Rounding or export issues require correction; the client described these as lower priority.

items.title: Payment delays affect payroll planning
items.description: Owners report concern that returned invoices delay the cash needed for wages.

groups.title: Payroll preparation and completion
groups.introduction: Payroll combines source checks, worker-specific adjustments and entry into the external payroll process.

items.title: Manual pay run configuration
items.description: Period dates, payment dates and payment methods require checking. Weekly/fortnightly wording in the transcript remains unclear.

items.title: Employee list cleanup
items.description: Inactive workers can remain in payroll selection and need review.

items.title: New starter setup
items.description: Adding an employee requires a separate payroll setup process whose complete steps were not supplied.

items.title: Previous run values
items.description: Staff inspect and refresh information carried over from earlier payslips. The field described as a base rate needs verification.

items.title: Worker by worker reconciliation
items.description: Staff compare ShiftCare hours and mileage with payroll inputs and manually enter the approved values.

items.title: Missing timesheets
items.description: Incomplete source records require investigation before payroll can proceed.

items.title: Adjustment tracking
items.description: Hour changes and exceptions must be found in notes and applied to the correct period.

items.title: Leave verification
items.description: Staff check requests, supporting documents, balances and the applicable payroll treatment.

items.title: Back pay entry
items.description: Corrections require calculations, approval, entry and explanatory notes.

items.title: Mileage interpretation
items.description: Kilometres, reimbursement amounts and payroll fields require careful distinction; the transcript does not establish a reimbursement rate.

items.title: Unconfirmed travel treatment
items.description: Home-to-first-job changes need an approved decision and communication before application.

items.title: Manual payroll completion
items.description: Staff save, finalize and email payslips employee by employee in the external payroll process.

groups.title: Service quality and case handling
groups.introduction: Reported service concerns need an owned response and enough evidence for a responsible person to make a decision.

items.title: Reported incomplete work
items.description: Owners describe missed tasks, inconsistent cleaning and early departures requiring investigation; these are reported concerns about service delivery.

items.title: Important information buried in notes
items.description: Significant events and extra time must be found among routine visit records, including restricted office notes.

items.title: Manual participant feedback
items.description: Staff arrange calls to learn how services are going.

items.title: Reactive problem discovery
items.description: The supervisor wants proactive feedback so concerns can be raised before relying on incoming complaints.

items.title: Fragmented complaint histories
items.description: Relevant explanations and correspondence must be assembled from several sources.

items.title: Pending personnel cases
items.description: Calls, voicemail, replies, management decisions and replacement arrangements must be coordinated.

items.title: Safety follow-up
items.description: Reported household hazards require reviewed communication and coordinated action with the appropriate people.

groups.title: People training and access
groups.introduction: Staff readiness depends on usable instructions, supervised practice, working tools and verified access.

items.title: Scattered procedural knowledge
items.description: Staff rely on personal notes and long recordings to recover instructions.

items.title: Repeated explanations
items.description: Supervisors revisit procedures when knowledge has not been retained.

items.title: Owner led training burden
items.description: New staff require substantial direct instruction and supervision.

items.title: Telephone coaching
items.description: Staff need observed practice, recording reviews, feedback and readiness checks.

items.title: Incomplete task sequencing
items.description: Staff can move to another task before finishing the required updates and follow-ups.

items.title: Unverified policy understanding
items.description: Supplying documents does not establish that staff read or understood them.

items.title: Delayed application access
items.description: Missing invitations, permissions, credentials or instructions prevent independent work.

items.title: Phone configuration work
items.description: Office-number access, licences, caller identity, routing and voicemail require setup and confirmation of the actual account configuration.

items.title: Group administration
items.description: Communication groups require membership, privacy boundaries and ownership decisions.

items.title: Audio faults
items.description: Microphone and call settings interrupt participant communication and training.

items.title: Unclear meeting identities
items.description: Generic accounts can make it difficult to establish who is present during sensitive discussions.

items.title: Manual absence history reconstruction
items.description: Managers search communication and roster records to establish factual absence histories; interpretation requires human review.

items.title: Incomplete offboarding
items.description: Former staff can remain on the website or payroll lists, requiring coordinated status and access review.

groups.title: Business pressures and owner dependency
groups.introduction: These reported business constraints influence automation priorities and the operating changes needed alongside software.

items.title: Dependence on the owners
items.description: Routine questions, exceptions, callbacks and approvals repeatedly return to the owners.

items.title: Difficulty stepping away
items.description: Owners report that operations become less reliable when they are unavailable.

items.title: Recruitment and backup pool maintenance
items.description: Applications require screening, practical assessment, availability checks and training; a reliable backup pool still needs people.

items.title: Lost service revenue
items.description: Uncovered or cancelled services reduce revenue while recurring costs remain, according to the meeting discussion.

items.title: Pressure from administration and subscriptions
items.description: Existing costs constrain decisions about adding support staff.

items.title: Limited marketing capacity
items.description: Owners lack time or specialist knowledge to maintain consistent promotion.

items.title: Variable demand
items.description: Holidays and uneven enquiry volumes complicate staffing and growth planning.

items.title: Supplier coordination
items.description: Website changes, email licences, renewals and provider communication require management time.

items.title: Memory based planning
items.description: Holiday closures and future follow-ups depend on notes and someone remembering to raise them.

items.title: Risk of adding duplicated work
items.description: The client wants improvements around existing ShiftCare functions without creating another repetitive workflow.

questions.title: Payroll calendar
questions.text: Resolve the weekly versus fortnightly wording and confirm the approved start/end dates, payment date and method.

questions.title: Previous payslip field
questions.text: Verify the screen field described as base rate before defining a reset procedure. The text does not authorize zeroing a contractual wage rate.

questions.title: Travel and mileage rules
questions.text: Confirm hour adjustments, mileage units and reimbursement treatment, plus any home-to-first-job policy and its communication/effective date.

questions.title: Intake date
questions.text: Identify whether the missing field is a submission, service, consultation or other date before changing the form.

questions.title: Certificate task
questions.text: Identify the certificate types, emailed request, filing destination and completion criteria. The brief reference does not establish the full workflow.

questions.title: Report preparation
questions.text: Clarify the briefly mentioned report, its period, inputs, audience and due time.

questions.title: Employee contract
questions.text: Clarify the contract fragment before defining any creation, signing or filing workflow.
